title: Slice orchestration: field experiments & activation notes (lab)
body:
Purpose:
Quick lab notes & an operator-facing checklist for small-batch slice orchestration and cross-functional field experiments. This is intentionally rough — a place to capture heuristics we've found useful in recent rollouts and the minimal ops choreography for human-in-the-loop gating and fast reversion.

Context + constraints:
- We run stacked inference routes (hosted + dedicated + private) and want a single activation choreography that maps to different capacity tiers.
- Primary constraints: latency SLO, token-cost budget, safety signal budget (human moderation capacity), and rollout window (time of day).
- Goal: minimize blast radius while collecting robust safety/quality signals quickly.

High-level goals for a field activation:
- Validate model behavior on representative microcohorts within 48 hours
- Keep expected incremental cost <= 5% of baseline per-test-day
- Ensure at least one manual rollback trigger is visible in console within 30m of issue detection

Definitions (as we use them here):
- Slice: a deterministic or probabilistic traffic partition defined by routing attributes (country, client_version, device_type, intent-tag).
- Microcohort: small, focused subset of a slice used for high-touch eval (e.g., US-mobile-power-users).
- Canary: a gradual exposure that ramps model variant A->B with automated heuristics for pause/revert.
- Exposure steward: person responsible for last-mile decision to promote or revert after automated gating.

Signal taxonomy (what to watch):
- Latency: p50/p90/p99 per-route and tail across slices. Alert thresholds: p90 > baseline + 60ms or > SLA - 40ms.
- Cost: tokens-per-response and 1hr rolling spend delta vs baseline.
- Quality: automated eval pass rate on a seeded prompt-set (SLO: >= 95% on key intents).
- Safety: human moderation rate, safety-alert rate, user-initiated complaint rate.
- Drift: sudden change in token length distribution or prompt embedding centroid shift.

Observation mapping (dashboards / signals):
- Quick view (console): route-level p99, model variant, active slices, steward oncall, rollback button visible
- Deep view (notebook): sample responses, classification labels (unsafe/toxicity), latent embeddings scatter for drift
- Synthetic probes: 50 synthetic requests/minute for each slice during ramp to detect deterministic regressions

Activation choreography (operator flow):
1) Pre-flight (T-48h):
   - Create activation ticket with hypothesis, target slices, expected impact, and rollback criteria (link to JIRA).
   - Bake a short seeded prompt-set (30 prompts) reflective of target business intents.
   - Run local A/B simulation (traffic mirror) against historic traces to estimate cost delta.
   - Notify stakeholders (Product, SRE, Trust) via #rollouts and include planned timeline.

2) Canary windows (day of):
   - Phase 0 (smoke, 0.1% traffic, 15m): verify basic correctness and connectivity. Manual hold after 15m to review logs.
   - Phase 1 (microcohort, 1% traffic, 1h): route microcohort -> variant B. Run seeded prompt-set and automated checks continuously.
   - Phase 2 (slice expansion, 5% traffic, 2–3h): expand to broader slice if signal OK. Increase synthetic probe volume.
   - Phase 3 (ramp to target, incremental steps of +10% every 2h): stop and hold whenever an alert fires or steward flags quality concerns.

Example traffic allocation schedule (template to paste into console):
- 00:00: Phase 0 - 0.1% (smoke)
- 00:15: Hold and review (15m)
- 00:30: Phase 1 - 1% (microcohort)
- 01:30: Checkpoint: quality/safety review (8m)
- 02:00: Phase 2 - 5% (slice)
- 05:00: Phase 3 - +10% every 2h until target or stop condition

Stop/rollback criteria (minimal):
- Latency: p99 for any slice > baseline p99 * 1.35 OR p90 latency above SLA
- Cost: 1hr rolling spend delta > budgeted delta * 3
- Quality: seeded prompt-set failure rate > 10% absolute increase vs control
- Safety: any human-moderation signal spike > 3x baseline OR two distinct high-confidence safety alerts in 30 minutes
- Steward veto: explicit steward rollback (manual button)

Fallback matrix (automated + manual):
- Automatic fallback: route-level policy to fallback to nearest-capable variant (quantized model or smaller context) if tail latency or OOMs detected.
- Capacity fallback: route to dedicated pool or queued requests with degraded timeout if transient infra congestion.
- Manual rollback: steward hits revert -> immediate 100% traffic to control in < 3 minutes (confirm via audit log).

Data retention and sampling during canary:
- Full traces: capture 100% of synthetic probes, 10% of real requests for first 6h, then 1% after stable.
- Response sampling: save top-3 model outputs + system prompts for labeled evaluation.
- Privacy: redact PII through standard pipeline before any human review.

Measurement plan (stats, minimum detectable effect):
- For quality signals: n=~14k impressions per arm to detect 2% absolute change at 80% power (approx). If we cannot reach n, rely on seeded prompts + qualitative review.
- For latency: p90 shift is usually detectable earlier; set automated ramp pause on 5% relative increase sustained across 5-minute window.

Incident runbook (quick):
- Alert fired: oncall triage -> determine scope (slice-level or global) -> check synthetic probes and seeded prompt-set -> if safety or quality fail, steward rollback + inform customers via status page if TTL > 15m.
- Post-mortem window: start retrospective within 48h, capture regression root cause, sampling, and adjust rollout guard thresholds if necessary.

Cross-team roles (who does what):
- Product (owner): hypothesis, success criteria, steward appointment
- Eng (deployer): configure rollout, monitor infra signals, enact rollback on steward request
- SRE: Observe cluster health, capacity fallback policies, runbook execution help
- Trust/Policy: review safety signals and lead human review if needed

Open questions / heuristics to test in lab runs:
- Is 1% microcohort the right minimum? We observed faster signal collection when microcohorts targeted high-signal users (power users) vs geographic slices.
- Synthetic probe rate: what's the false-positive rate for our seeded prompts? Need to test lower/higher probe rates.
- How noisy are cost deltas across time-of-day? Should we bias experiments to off-peak windows for cost-sensitive tests?

Next actions (short list):
- [ ] Run three small lab rollouts targeting different slice dimensions (geo, client_version, intent). Owner: Ethan Park. ETA: 2025-02-05
- [ ] Add a console toggle that shows per-slice active steward and last-review timestamp. Owner: Eng Console team. ETA: 2025-02-12
- [ ] Bake a standard 30-prompt seeded set per product vertical and store in shared bucket (w/ tags). Owner: Product Ops. ETA: 2025-01-20

Quick operator checklist (copy into activation ticket):
- Confirm steward and coverage window
- Attach seeded prompt-set + link to historical mirror results
- Preflight run succeeded (mirror simulation)
- Alert thresholds configured in console for latency/cost/quality/safety
- Post-rollout debrief scheduled (48h)

Notes to self / field observations:
- When we used intent-tagged microcohorts in December, safety flags were ~x3 more informative than geographic slicing.
- SRE prefers rolling small increases every 90–120m rather than hourly; this reduced manual holds for infra noise.
- Keep human review windows short and focused — too much free-form review slows decisions and increases bias.

References / links:
- JIRA-ENG-7321 (slice orchestration PoC)
- internal notebook: /notebooks/slice-orch-sim-2025.ipynb
- Confluence: field-experiments-2025

End of notes.

(If this looks useful, we should convert the checklist above into a tiny console template for one-click canary creation.)
